descriptionSections.content: If a private field is declared but not used locally, it is dead code and should be removed. This helps maintainability because developers will not wonder what the field is used for.

Remove the unused field, or if it is assigned by a framework (e.g. dependency injection), use it or mark it appropriately.

Noncompliant code example

public class MyClass {
  private int foo = 42;  // Noncompliant: foo is unused
}

Compliant solution

public class MyClass {
}

rule.name: Unused local variables should be removed

descriptionSections.content: An unused local variable is dead code. It clutters the method, confuses readers, and can hide bugs where the wrong variable is used instead.

Remove the declaration of the unused variable.

Noncompliant code example

int total = 0;  // Noncompliant: never read
return rows.size();

Compliant solution

return rows.size();
Connections, streams, files, and other classes that implement Closeable or AutoCloseable need to be closed after use. Failing to do so leaks resources and can exhaust file handles under load.

Use the try-with-resources statement so the resource is closed automatically.

Noncompliant code example

FileInputStream in = new FileInputStream(path); // Noncompliant
byte[] data = in.readAllBytes();
return data;

Compliant solution

try (FileInputStream in = new FileInputStream(path)) {
  return in.readAllBytes();
}
